stem: A client taking carbamazepine develops new dizziness, diplopia, and unsteady coordination. What is the nurse’s best interpretation?

options.A: These are recognized neurologic adverse effects of carbamazepine and warrant medication-safety assessment.
options.B: They are expected evidence of improved seizure control and need no further assessment.
options.C: They are unrelated to carbamazepine because the drug does not affect vision or coordination.
options.D: They establish an inner-ear disorder and should be treated without reviewing the medication regimen.

rationale: The current DailyMed carbamazepine extended-release label lists dizziness and unsteadiness among the most frequently observed adverse reactions and lists disturbances of coordination, blurred vision, and transient diplopia among nervous-system adverse reactions. New dizziness, diplopia, and unsteady coordination therefore warrant assessment as possible medication adverse effects. A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize dizziness, diplopia and impaired coordination as known carbamazepine neurologic adverse effects that require medication-safety assessment.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine official drug label
source_version_date: DailyMed version 12, updated February 19, 2026; prescribing information revised February 2026
source_locator: Adverse Reactions: most frequently observed adverse reactions include dizziness and unsteadiness; Nervous System adverse reactions include dizziness, disturbances of coordination, blurred vision, and transient diplopia.
source_claim_supported: Dizziness, unsteadiness/coordination disturbance, blurred vision and transient diplopia are recognized carbamazepine adverse reactions and should prompt medication-safety assessment when newly present.

correction_summary: Retained key A and the neurologic-adverse-effect construct, corrected the exact DailyMed update date to February 19, 2026 for version 12, preserved the direct label-supported symptom set, and reduced difficulty from hard to easy because the final item is straightforward adverse-effect recognition.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current DailyMed version 12 official label; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.exact_locator: DailyMed Adverse Reactions and Nervous System subsections
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses only directly listed neurologic adverse effects and appropriately frames them as warranting assessment rather than proving toxicity or another diagnosis.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because adverse effects are not evidence of therapeutic seizure control.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because the label explicitly lists visual and coordination disturbances.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because the symptom cluster does not establish an inner-ear diagnosis and medication review is clinically relevant.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A accurately links all three new findings to the medication label without overdiagnosis.
audit_findings.cueing: All options interpret the same post-medication neurologic findings.
audit_findings.blueprint: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — adverse-effect recognition and monitoring.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read DailyMed version 12, confirmed exact update date and listed neurologic effects, then rechecked all options, rationale and blueprint mapping. A remained uniquely correct.
